solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable copy, its numbering matching the numbers printed in it and the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Direction finder in the sky as part shifts with cosmos

indicators.note: shifts says the letters of the three words move around into a new order

explanation.surface: An instrument for navigating by the stars is described as a bit of the cosmos moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' only joins the scrambled words to what comes before.
explanation.definitionFit: An astrocompass is a navigational instrument that finds direction from the positions of stars, so it is a direction finder using the sky.

clue.text: Get tight, creating a mess

explanation.surface: Someone getting drunk and making a hash of things.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense is to tighten by screwing; the noun sense is a bungle. 'creating' just joins the two.
explanation.definitionFit: To screw something up is to tighten it, and a screw-up is a blunder or muddle.

clue.text: Critical commentary's making one irritated when bound in sticky stuff

indicators.note: bound in means one piece is enclosed by the sticky stuff, sitting inside it

parts.note: mastic is a gummy resin or adhesive
sore can describe something that rankles, as in a sore point

explanation.surface: A critic's remarks are so annoying they feel like being stuck in glue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' belongs with 'one irritated', as in a sore point, rather than acting as a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Massoretic means relating to the Massorah, the body of critical notes on the text of the Hebrew Bible, so it is the adjective for that commentary.

clue.text: Potato coating two thirds of crusty dish at most (5, two words)

indicators.note: coating means the potato word wraps round the trimmed dish

parts.note: alu (aloo) is the Indian word for potato

indicators.note: two thirds of a three-letter word keeps two letters and drops the last

parts.note: a pie is a dish with a pastry crust

explanation.surface: A recipe says the potato should cover most of the pie dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is an Italian musical direction, entered as two words. Alu is the Indian kitchen word for potato, familiar from dishes like aloo gobi.
explanation.definitionFit: Al più is an Italian phrase, used in music, meaning no more than or at the most.

clue.text: Blended sherry casks are inverted under sun

indicators.note: in a down entry, under places the following letters below the sun word

parts.note: sol is Latin for sun, and the name of the sun as a deity

indicators.note: inverted turns the word are upside down, which in a down light reads it from the bottom

explanation.surface: Sherry barrels are turned over and left in the sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inverted' turns ARE into ERA, which 'under' places below SOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A solera is a tiered system of casks in which sherries of different ages are blended.

clue.text: See vegan mistreated in series totter?

indicators.note: in places the letters before it inside the abbreviation for series

parts.note: C stands for see, as in text-speak C U

indicators.note: mistreated means the letters of vegan are handled roughly into a new order

explanation.surface: A vegan is badly treated in a run of programmes about a wobbly character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'totter' is not a wobbly walker but a rag-and-bone collector, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A totter is a rag-and-bone man who picks over refuse for saleable items, a kind of scavenger.

clue.text: Followers of the rest in your arcane religion many renounce, as of old

indicators.note: the letters that come after the rest of each word are the final letters of those four words

explanation.surface: Converts to an obscure faith are urged by many to give it up.
explanation.definitionFit: Reny is an obsolete form of renay, meaning to deny or forswear something.

clue.text: Is etching of Parisian in love?

indicators.note: in puts the French word inside the god of love

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love
de is French for of

explanation.surface: A question about whether a Paris print is a romantic one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'etching' looks like a noun about artwork; read it as a verb, wearing away.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear away gradually, as acid does when it etches metal.

clue.text: Old militiaman, game character embraced by girl

indicators.note: embraced by means the game hero is held inside the girl word

parts.note: tit is an old dialect word for a girl or young woman
Mario is the plumber hero of Nintendo video games

explanation.surface: A video-game figure is hugged by a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A timariot was a feudal cavalryman of the Ottoman Empire who held land in return for military service.

clue.text: Deliveries, costings worked out, number fellows packed

indicators.note: packed means the second group of letters is stuffed inside the first
worked out says the letters of costings are reorganised

parts.note: men are fellows, chaps

explanation.surface: Shipping costs have been calculated, with a number of staff loaded aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked out' and 'packed' both read as accountancy and luggage talk, disguising the anagram and the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A consignment is a batch of goods sent or delivered, so consignments are deliveries.

clue.text: Shoddy item from school cupboard

parts.note: a locker is a small lockable cupboard

explanation.surface: Some cheap rubbish was found in a pupil's locker.
explanation.definitionFit: Schlock is cheap, inferior goods, and a schlocker is a shoddy thing of that kind.

clue.text: Restraining strap from timeless jokes

indicators.note: timeless means without T, the abbreviation for time

parts.note: jests are jokes

explanation.surface: A leash made from jokes that never date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' looks like praise for old jokes; it drops the T from JESTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A jess is the short leather strap fastened to a hawk's leg in falconry to hold it.

clue.text: Test with probe initially revealing parasite

parts.note: to try is to test

indicators.note: initially picks only the opening letter of probe

explanation.surface: A lab trial with a probe uncovers a parasite.
explanation.definitionFit: Tryp is short for trypanosome, a parasitic protozoan that causes sleeping sickness.

clue.text: International banker invested in anonymous label?

indicators.note: invested in means the banker is put inside the abbreviation

parts.note: anon. abbreviates anonymous, and An. is also used
the Gnomes of Zurich was a jibe at Swiss international bankers

explanation.surface: A global financier puts money into a nameless brand.
explanation.walkthrough: The financial sense of 'invested' hides an insertion; 'banker' is not a river here but a gnome.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnomen is an extra name or nickname added to a person's name, a label attached to them.

clue.text: A real challenge for climbers, reversing government monopoly

indicators.note: reversing reads the mountain's name backwards

parts.note: the Eiger is a Swiss peak whose north face is notoriously hard to climb

explanation.surface: A mountaineering challenge is linked to a state monopoly backing down.
explanation.definitionFit: A régie is a state-controlled monopoly, as of tobacco or salt in France.

clue.text: Plantation refuse, a difficulty in economic collapse

indicators.note: in puts the first pair of pieces inside the collapse word

parts.note: a crash is a sudden collapse of markets or the economy
a net, a snare or entanglement, is a difficulty one is caught in

explanation.surface: Farm waste is just one more problem in a financial crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'economic' looks like part of the definition's world of farm accounts; it only qualifies the collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: Cane trash is the crushed stalks and leaves left after sugar cane is processed on a plantation.

clue.text: Titania's swain? Only a bit

indicators.note: only a bit means just a short run of the letters of the phrase is taken

explanation.surface: Titania's lover in A Midsummer Night's Dream was only partly an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across Titania's and swain. In Shakespeare's play Titania dotes on Bottom, who has only an ass's head, so he is only a bit of one.
explanation.definitionFit: Titania falls for Bottom while he wears a donkey's head, so her beloved is a donkey.

clue.text: Old soldier with no lance in section poorly paid, see

indicators.note: poorly means the letters of paid and see are badly arranged

explanation.surface: A veteran without his weapon is badly paid, you see.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cute: an old lancepesade or lanspeisade is a lance corporal, and taking away the lance part leaves this word.
explanation.definitionFit: Speisade is a shortened form of lancepesade, an old term for a lance corporal, the low-ranking soldier.

clue.text: Combines school latrine with built-in gym?

indicators.note: with built-in says the gym letters are placed inside the toilet word

parts.note: rears is old school slang for lavatories
PE, physical education, is school gym

explanation.surface: A school block puts the toilets and a gym together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Combines' looks like a verb; it is the plural noun, harvesting machines.
explanation.definitionFit: Reapers are harvesting machines, and a combine is a machine that reaps and threshes.

clue.text: Fellow drinker putting money into copper dish

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: putting into means the money letter goes inside the dish
putting into means the money letter goes inside the dish

parts.note: a pan is a shallow dish
M is short for money, as in M1 and M3 measures

explanation.surface: A drinking companion drops coins into a copper bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupman is a boon companion who drinks with you, a fellow drinker.

clue.text: University sportswear let out for exercising

indicators.note: out means the word let is removed from the garment

parts.note: a singlet is a sleeveless vest worn for athletics

explanation.surface: A college's sports kit has been loosened for working out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let out' reads as tailoring, loosening a garment; here LET is taken out of SINGLET.
explanation.definitionFit: Using a faculty or tool means employing or exercising it.

clue.text: Former vacation, not something you'd find in Oxford's vocabulary?

definitions.text: not something you'd find in Oxford's vocabulary?

explanation.surface: An old holiday period and a word Oxford would never use.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford University has terms, so a 'not-term' would be no part of its vocabulary; the question mark marks that playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-term was an old name for a university vacation, the time between terms.

clue.text: Hardwood tree does when peeled — go inside

indicators.note: inside means the energy word goes within the peeled word
peeled strips off the outer letters of does, leaving its middle

parts.note: go and pep both mean energy, vigour

explanation.surface: A tree says to skin it and then climb inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Opepe is a West African tree yielding a hard, durable yellowish timber.

clue.text: Old-fashioned dive, for some time closed by police, empty

indicators.note: closed by means the time word is shut in by the outer letters
empty removes the inside of police, leaving its first and last letters

parts.note: long means for a considerable time

explanation.surface: A seedy old dive was shut down by police and left empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dive' looks like a seedy bar; it is a plunge into water.
explanation.definitionFit: Plonge is an obsolete word for a plunge or dive.

clue.text: Shifting ooze covering ancient fossil possibly

indicators.note: shifting moves the letters of ooze into another order

parts.note: on means placed over, covering something

explanation.surface: Moving slime covers an old fossil.
explanation.definitionFit: Eozoon was a structure in ancient rocks once claimed as the oldest fossil, though it proved mineral, hence possibly.

clue.text: Become absorbed in bit of marrow in two bones, carcase's last

indicators.note: this in puts the marrow letter between the two bones

parts.note: os is Latin for bone, used twice

indicators.note: a bit of marrow is just its opening letter
last picks the final letter of carcase

explanation.surface: Getting stuck into the marrow from a pair of bones at the end of a carcase.
explanation.definitionFit: To osmose is to pass through a membrane by osmosis, being absorbed gradually.

clue.text: Skittish lassies, reprehensible with Scots kids around

indicators.note: around means the Scots word wraps round the bad word

parts.note: gets is a Scots word for brats or children
ill can mean bad or wicked

explanation.surface: Flighty girls behave badly with Scottish children about.
explanation.definitionFit: Gillet is a Scots word for a giddy young woman, so gillets are flighty girls.

clue.text: High whatsit, but not thin

indicators.note: but not means the following word is removed from the first

parts.note: thingamy is a name for something whose name escapes you
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tall thing, but a stout one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' means tall in the surface; it is meat that has begun to go off.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamy meat smells strongly of game, as when hung until high or slightly tainted.

clue.text: Judicial decision, mostly deadly when woman's involved

indicators.note: involved means the woman letter is wrapped inside the shortened word
mostly drops the last letter of the word for deadly

parts.note: fatal means deadly
W is the abbreviation for woman

explanation.surface: A court ruling is nearly lethal once a woman is mixed up in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatwa is a ruling on a point of Islamic law given by a qualified jurist.

clue.text: Action course avoided by sage

indicators.note: avoided by means the herb word is left out of the course word

parts.note: a passage is a course or route

explanation.surface: A course of action is shunned by a wise man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sage' looks like a wise person; it is just the four letters removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pas is a step or movement in dancing, the action of a dance passage.

clue.text: Seaweed one's left dug into bed

indicators.note: dug into means the letter for left is buried inside the bed word

parts.note: kip is slang for a bed or sleep

explanation.surface: A piece of seaweed is buried in a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' means the answer has: the seaweed has left in its bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Kilp is a variant spelling of kelp, a large brown seaweed.

clue.text: Mask concealing final character in affair

indicators.note: concealing the final character means the last letter of the word is hidden away

parts.note: a matter is an affair or business

explanation.surface: A disguise hides the last person involved in an affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' suggests a person in a story; it is the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In film, a matte is a mask used to block part of the image so another can be combined with it.

clue.text: Mushroom? Sounds a bit like one chaps should avoid!

indicators.note: sounds a bit like says the phrase, said aloud, is close to the answer

parts.note: a man-eater is a woman who devours men, so men should steer clear

explanation.surface: A dangerous mushroom is jokingly compared to a predatory woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Amanita is a genus of mushrooms including the deadly death cap and fly agaric.

clue.text: Article given number immediately

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: An essay is assigned a number at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Then can mean at that moment, straight away, so it is an old sense of at once.

clue.text: Plant yielding soda salt grows wild

indicators.note: wild says the letters of salt and grows run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A salt-marsh plant grows rampantly.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasswort, or samphire, is a salt-marsh plant whose ashes were burned for soda used in glassmaking.

clue.text: Yank's fish he cooked with peas in outhouse (10, apostrophe)

indicators.note: in puts the cooked mixture inside the outhouse word

parts.note: a shed is an outhouse

indicators.note: cooked means the letters of he and peas are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone prepares a fish dish with peas in a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank's' marks the fish as an American name; the sheep's-head is not a dish of offal here.
explanation.definitionFit: The sheep's-head is a North American food fish, a sea bream with blunt teeth.
